clue.text: Warning protest against wearing fewer clothes

parts.note: to object is to protest against something
someone wearing fewer clothes has less on

explanation.surface: A protester warns against people going about scantily dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece splits as LESS ON: having less on means wearing fewer clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson taught by example is a cautionary warning to others.

clue.text: Ill-natured gossip with piece mounted by angel

indicators.note: in this down clue the angel's word straddles the piece, carried around it as if riding it

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a show
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip pairs up with a cherub perched on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' is theatre slang for a financial backer, not a heavenly being; 'mounted by' suits a down clue, the angel's word sitting astride the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbiter is a person who speaks spitefully about others behind their backs, a malicious gossip.

clue.text: Lyre that is played in weird style

indicators.note: a lyre that is played makes its notes rearrange, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A lyre strummed so as to sound uncanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' shuffles LYRE plus IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something uncannily, in a strange and spooky manner.

clue.text: Virtual piece about female with great and swell

indicators.note: the fragment of Virtual is wrapped about the word for a female
only a piece of the word Virtual is used, its tail end

parts.note: the last part of the word Virtual
a woman is a female

explanation.surface: A virtual composition concerning a woman who is both great and swell.
explanation.walkthrough: Great and swell are names of organ keyboards, not compliments; 'Virtual piece' means just a fragment of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ having two keyboards, typically the great and the swell manuals, is described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: See 1
Ghastly old city in cover

indicators.note: the old city sits in the cover, inside its letters

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A grim ancient city lies under some covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid can mean shockingly gruesome or horrifying, a synonym of ghastly.

clue.text: Slightly less than blues composer, as entered

indicators.note: the Latin word has entered the rearranged letters, going inside them
a composer arranges notes, so the letters of blues are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
qua is Latin for 'as', in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Something falls just short of a blues songwriter, as recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' rearranges BLUES to SUBEL; QUA (as) is 'entered' into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Subequal is a technical term for nearly equal, that is very slightly smaller in size or amount.

clue.text: In place of petrol, diesel seems somewhat dated

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun: an old-timer or old song is a dated thing

indicators.note: only some of the letters of petrol, diesel are taken, run on from one word into the next

explanation.surface: Using diesel in place of petrol seems a bit old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' signals the run of letters spanning petrOL DIEsel.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person, song or film, something dated or from a past era.

clue.text: Was the pact here to look at the registration number?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, behold
the car number, the registration number on a car's plate

explanation.surface: A question whether a treaty was signed where someone checked a licence plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Locarno Pact of 1925 was signed in Locarno, Switzerland; the wordplay splits as LO + CAR NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Locarno Treaties of 1925 were negotiated in this Swiss lakeside town, giving its name to the pact.

clue.text: Enslavement, perhaps, in classical book, "Bond circumvents detectives"

parts.note: liber is Latin for book

indicators.note: the bond goes round the detectives, enclosing them

parts.note: a tie is a bond
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A James Bond book title in Latin style, with Bond dodging the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007, and the quoted phrase like a novel title, but Bond is a plain synonym and CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberticide means the destruction of liberty, of which enslaving people is one example.

clue.text: Polish capital (back half) on a roll

parts.note: to rub is to polish

indicators.note: the remaining half of the capital is turned back to front
Budapest is made of two halves, Buda and Pest, and only one half is kept

parts.note: Budapest is the Hungarian capital

explanation.surface: The Polish capital seen rolling backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps BUDA of BUDAPEST; 'back' turns it to ADUB. 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rub-a-dub imitates the sound of a drum roll, so the term names such a roll.

clue.text: Greek art: terrible I from Russia perplexed detective's assistants

indicators.note: perplexed means muddled, so the pooled letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Greek art and a terrible tsar from Russia leave a sleuth's helpers baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool GREEK ART, TERRIBLE and RUSSIA, take away I ('from'), and 'perplexed' rearranges the rest. 'Terrible I' suggests Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baker Street Irregulars were street urchins who helped Sherlock Holmes with his investigations.

clue.text: Basque bank blued allowance from vegetable dish

indicators.note: an allowance is latitude or leeway, so the letters are given freedom to move into a new order

explanation.surface: A Basque bank spent the allowance it took from a vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blued' is slang for spent, squandered; here all three words are the fodder. BUBBLE AND SQUEAK is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a fried dish of leftover cabbage and potato, a traditional vegetable dish.

clue.text: The girl Verity goes topless

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed, like a top taken off

parts.note: verity means truth

explanation.surface: A young woman named Verity goes about without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes topless' drops T from TRUTH. Verity is also a girl's name, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's first name, the heroine of the Old Testament book.

clue.text: Backwoodsman with jalopy keeping American time

indicators.note: the old car is keeping the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A frontiersman drives an old wreck while keeping US time.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a decrepit old car; a bushranger was originally an Australian outlaw living rough in the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushranger was an outlaw or person living in the Australian bush, someone of the backwoods.

clue.text: Watered around forest — no point in it? Tough!

indicators.note: the watering word goes around the shortened forest

parts.note: hosed means watered with a hose

indicators.note: the forest's name loses E, a compass point, from inside it

parts.note: Arden is the forest in Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: Someone waters around a forest with no apparent purpose and finds it tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is Shakespeare's forest in As You Like It; 'no point' is the usual signal to drop a compass letter, here E for East.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-nosed describes someone tough-minded and unsentimental, so the adjective is a synonym of tough.

clue.text: Water bird around yard, with the rest of it for 7

indicators.note: the bird's letters go around the abbreviation

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird
the remainder of the word yard after its first letter

explanation.surface: A water bird circling a yard is an old-timer.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter of yard sits inside the bird; 'the rest of it' follows on. 7 points to clue 7, whose answer is an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, which is one sense of the answer to clue 7.

clue.text: A place for a car, pointless when one has no topping or jelly

indicators.note: the word loses E, a compass point

parts.note: a garage is a place for keeping a car
a means one

indicators.note: the word or loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A garage spot is useless when a dessert has no topping or jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops E (East) from GARAGE; 'no topping' leaves R of 'or'. 'or' looks like a link; it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to make jelly and set foods.

clue.text: See 10
The other half from 9 is a nuisance

indicators.note: the remaining half of that capital is kept, with the half used in clue 9 removed

parts.note: clue 9 used the capital Budapest, keeping its first half

explanation.surface: Half of something is described as irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 9 used BUDA from BUDAPEST; this one takes the other half.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, a nuisance.

clue.text: Wheel for unEnglish boats?

indicators.note: un- negates English, so the boats are made un-English by losing their E, the abbreviation for English

parts.note: ferries are boats

explanation.surface: A wheel fitted to boats that are not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unEnglish' removes E (English) from FERRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferris wheel is the fairground big wheel, so the name stands for wheel.

clue.text: Virtually the same mess began in the clear

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the following letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone who made a mess got off scot-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' shuffles BEGAN IN THE CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are interchangeable can be swapped because they are effectively identical.

clue.text: Only just 8 + 1?

definitions.meaning: a ... result is won by a narrow margin, only just
'one over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk

explanation.walkthrough: 8 + 1 is not a cross-reference: it is 'one over the eight', British slang for being tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight means narrowly close, and also means drunk, as in one drink past eight.

clue.text: Barrier on the hard side

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an edge is a side

explanation.surface: A barrier sits on the tough side of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of bushes forming a boundary or barrier.

clue.text: Busy with a date?

definitions.meaning: a telephone line that is ... is busy
someone ... has a date booked, or is promised to be married

explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means occupied, and also means promised in marriage or booked for an appointment.

clue.text: Insert transport for underling

indicators.note: the clue's first word splits as In-sert, telling you to put the transport in SERT

parts.note: taken as written, the second part of Insert
a van is a form of transport

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a vehicle in place for a junior worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria splits the first word as 'In sert', so the transport is put in the second half of that word rather than inserted somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is someone who serves another, an underling or subordinate.

clue.text: Refrain from food and take in lines of music

indicators.note: the letter for take goes in the lines of music

parts.note: a stave is the set of five lines music is written on
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Fast from eating and absorb some sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' tempts as a musical chorus; it is the verb to abstain.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, abstaining from eating.

clue.text: Square-dance figure is turning into a dead thing

indicators.note: the turned word goes into the extinct bird's name

parts.note: the dodo is the proverbial dead thing, as dead as a dodo

indicators.note: the word is turns round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A square-dance move turns into something lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As dead as a dodo' is the idiom behind 'a dead thing'; the reversed 'is' sits in the middle of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The do-si-do is a figure in square dancing where partners circle back to back.
